title: You weren’t an accident.
paragraphs:
You weren’t an accident.
You were authored.
“So God created man in His own image, in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them.” — Genesis 1:27
Read that again.

Image.
Not imitation.
Not experiment.
Image.
You carry something eternal in your bones.
But here’s the tension…

If you’re made in God’s image,
why do you feel so broken?

Why the shame you hide?
Why the sin you can’t seem to outrun?
Why the quiet voice that whispers, “You’re not enough”?
Because the image was marred.

Not erased.
Marred.

Sin didn’t delete your worth—
it distorted your reflection.

And that distortion?
It separates us from the very God whose image we bear.
But here’s what we miss…

God didn’t abandon His image.
He came for it.
Through Jesus.

Jesus Christ didn’t just preach truth—He restored what was broken.
On the cross, He carried the full weight of our distortion—our sin, our rebellion, our shame.
So the image could breathe again.

So you could look in the mirror
and not just see failure—
but redemption in progress.
This is the Gospel:

You were created in God’s image.
You fell into sin.
But through Christ, you can be made new—fully restored, fully forgiven, fully His.

Not improved.
Redeemed.
So don’t settle for the lie that you’re worthless.

You are an image-bearer
being called back to the One you reflect.
Come home.

From distortion to glory—
because Jesus still restores what sin tried to ruin.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
